title: fix(scripts): the polarity census reads a key as a NAME, not as any lowercase token
body:
Fixes #9766

Clause-②: no

`Fixes`, not `Refs`: the card's whole face is discharged here — the `keyHead`
reader, the limits section of the instrument's header docblock, and the pin —
with nothing of it deferred. What is NOT discharged is named in Acceptance
notes, and none of it is on this card.

## The defect

`scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs`'s key reader admitted backticked tokens
that cannot be member keys: the language's own primitives and keywords, and call
expressions. The exclusion rule was written on one side only — a backticked
PascalCase token was named a TYPE and refused — and stopped at the lowercase
side, where `/^[a-z_$]/` waved everything through.

⚠️ These were invisible until objectui#9765 narrowed polarity to the clause. A
NEGATIVE reading only contradicts when the member is PRESENT, and a pseudo-key
is present on no face, so the old sentence-wide negation was suppressing them by
accident. ⇒ a defect objectui#9765 EXPOSED, ⛔ not one it introduced, and ⛔ not
a regression to undo.

## The rule, and why it is a rule rather than a list

Answering the question first — **in this protocol, what does a member key look
like?** — a member key is a NAME, and the backticked span has to BE that name.
The rule now lives on `keyHead`, where the PascalCase half already lived, and it
has three parts:

1. **The span IS the name.** A key is written bare (`columns`) or carrying its
   type annotation (`columns: KanbanColumn[]`, which names `columns`).
   Everything else in a backticked span is a fragment of CODE, not a name: a
   call, a heritage clause (the `extends Omit` form, its type arguments written
   in angle brackets — spelled in words here because GitHub's body sanitizer
   eats tag-shaped fragments), a statement (`export { A as B }`), an operator
   use (`as any`), a switch label, a path expression (`conditions[].operator`).
   ⭐ This removes the CONSTRUCTION that permitted the error: the reader used to
   CUT the span at its first separator and keep the head, which manufactured a
   name out of any of those. Only the annotation form is still cut.
2. **The name is spelled like a key.** One regex, `MEMBER_KEY_SPELLING`, fused
   from the two tests that used to run in sequence — so the correct shape is
   written once and is the only spelling that gets through.
3. **The name is the protocol's, not the language's.** ⭐ `string` and `size` are
   lexically identical, so no character class can separate them and this part is
   deliberately NOT lexical. A word the TypeScript compiler defines as a keyword
   is the language the faces are written in, not a key of the protocol they
   describe, so it is admitted only where the tree being read declares a member
   by that name. `type` is a key — the protocol's recursion point and this
   instrument's own member control — and stays one; `string`, `number`,
   `boolean`, `any` are keys of nothing and stop being read as keys.

**Why this is not a blacklist.** The word set is DERIVED at load time from the
`ts` the instrument already parses the faces with (`LANGUAGE_WORDS`), never
hand-typed, so it cannot go stale the way a written-down population does
(commandment #9) — and the pin asserts it carries `intrinsic`, `satisfies`,
`accessor` and `asserts`, which no one hand-lists from memory. A blacklist is
also not merely inelegant here, it is WRONG: it refuses `type`, the
most-declared key in the tree. That leg is pinned, and the ablation below shows
the blacklist spelling going red on it.

**And the gate is on language words ONLY, which is load bearing.** Applied to
every name it would suppress exactly the claim this instrument exists to catch —
a present-tense claim about a key the tree no longer declares anywhere, which is
objectui#9713's `allowCollapse`. That leg is pinned too, and the ablation shows
the wider spelling taking the objectui#9727 blind-spot fixture down with it.

## The census reading, before and after, each with its ref

`node scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` at objectui `57c07f002` (this
branch's merge-base with origin/main) printed **143 candidate contradictions
across 58 entries**; the same command at this branch's `31a96ea40` prints **118
across 55**. Controls PASS at both refs with identical readings, and the
population did not move at all: matched-ASSERTION, matched-QUOTED and
schema-not-declared all read the same at both refs, so the change is confined to
key extraction.

**27 flags removed, 2 added.** The removals, by which part of the rule refused
them (counts from a diff of the two `--json` runs at those two refs):

| refused because | keys |
| --- | --- |
| the span is not a name (call, heritage clause, statement, operator use, path expression) | `retirementTombstone` ×3, `export` ×2, `handlerKeyRefusal`, `extends`, `as`, `case`, `conditions`, `onNavigate`, `onAddComment` — 12 |
| a language word no face declares | `any` ×7, `string` ×3, `boolean` ×2, `number` ×2, `namespace` — 15 |

**The 2 additions are the interesting half, and the count rose there for a good
reason.** Both are `safeParse` in one entry, and both carry the
marker for an object reached across a sentence boundary. The sentence's only
backticked "key" was `any`; with `any` no longer a key the sentence carries none
of its own, its object is a pronoun, and the cross-sentence pronoun reader that
objectui#9727 added fires where it was previously pre-empted. The instrument's own
pronoun-resolution reading moves 9 → 10 between those two refs, which is that
account's corroboration. ⇒ a mechanism was unblocked, not a false positive
invented — though the key it lands on is itself the lexical residue this PR
names in the header.

**Two costs, named rather than hidden.** `namespace` is a genuine registry key
that happens to be a TypeScript keyword and is declared on no face under
`packages/types/src`, so the language-word part drops it; its three sibling keys
in the same sentence still flag, so the finding survives. And `onNavigate` /
`onAddComment` are real key names written as call signatures — a span written as
a signature is no longer read as a key mention.

## ⛔ Precision was not bought with blindness

The instrument's pinned blind-spot fixture — the pre-repair text of the site
that motivated objectui#9727 — returns **exactly the four keys objectui#9713
adjudicated, 4 before and 4 after**, every one reached across a sentence
boundary, measured by running the fixture census under both the `57c07f002`
module and this branch's in the same process. Three would have meant the
instrument was broken rather than sharpened. It is asserted twice: by the
existing pin 1 and again by a pin that names it as THIS card's acceptance
condition.

## Every pin shown failing, restore proven

Seven mutation legs, each: mutate → prove the text reached disk (anchor and
injected-text occurrence counts, ⛔ never an editor's exit code) → run → restore
with `git checkout HEAD --` → prove the restore by blob hash equal to HEAD's and
by `git diff HEAD` empty. The harness carried a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restore
throughout and treats an empty hash as FAILURE. Control run on the unmutated
tree at `31a96ea40`: 38 passed, 0 failed.

| leg | mutation | pins that went RED |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | restore the cut-at-first-separator construction | refuses every span that is code; end-to-end fixture |
| B | delete the language-word gate | refuses a language word; LEG 1; end-to-end |
| C | make it a KEYWORD BLACKLIST (ignore what the tree declares) | LEG 1 (`type`); end-to-end |
| D | widen the gate to EVERY name (corroboration required) | 9 red, incl. LEG 2 and the objectui#9727 pronoun mechanism |
| E | re-admit PascalCase in the key spelling | 12 red, incl. the blind-spot fixture and its four keys |
| F | hand-list the language words instead of deriving them | the DERIVED pin; refuses a language word; LEG 1 |
| G | empty the vocabulary `declaredNames` builds | the vocabulary-is-not-membership pin; LEG 1 |

Every legs' restore printed the same blob hash as `HEAD:scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs`
and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

## Changeset: none owed, and the grade is MEASURED

Corpus: every path enumerated by the `files` array of all 39 publishable
packages that exists on disk after `pnpm exec turbo run build --force`
(43 of 43 tasks successful) at `31a96ea40` — **152 paths**.

- **ABSENT control** — the symbols and paths this diff introduces
  (`MEMBER_KEY_SPELLING`, `LANGUAGE_WORDS`, `declaredNames`, `keyHead`,
  `changeset-polarity-census`, `08-key-extraction`): **0 files each**.
- **LIT control** — symbols that are certainly published: `SchemaRenderer`
  **224 files**, `BaseSchema` **113**, `registerComponent` **3**. The corpus is
  live and greppable, so the zeros above are readings and not a dead probe.
- Zero `files` entries escape their own package directory, so a repo-root
  `scripts/` file cannot ship by any route.

The repo's own authoritative instrument agrees: `node
scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exits 0 and prints that 0 of the changed
files are published source of a package the release covers.

⚠️ ⛔ **No empty-frontmatter changeset was added either, and that is a
deliberate deviation from the card's scope line, reported rather than silent.**
`.changeset/` IS this instrument's corpus: a file added there is a new entry in
every future census run, so declaring "no release" by writing into the corpus
would perturb the very reading this PR reports. The gate owes nothing, so
nothing was written.

## Verification

Run under the shared verify lock at `31a96ea40`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/changeset-polarity-census.test.ts` —
  38 passed (29 before this branch, 9 added).
- `pnpm run type-check:scripts` — exit 0.
- `pnpm run lint:root` — exit 0 (the population for a repo-root `scripts/` file;
  warnings only, none in the files this branch touches).
- Gates run green: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`,
  `check:entry-guard`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:shell-escape-residue`,
  `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:test-path-roots`,
  `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`,
  `check:changeset-claims`, `check:node-esm-load`.
- Control-character sweep over the three touched files: no hits.

## Acceptance notes

⛔ Out of scope and deliberately untouched, both separately carded: WINDOW
PAIRING (objectui#9754 slice 2) and the schema-absent report-line split
(objectui#9767). Neither was widened into.

⭐ One thing this PR bears on objectui#9754 slice 2, which its claim comment
already anticipated: this branch changes what counts as a key, so it changes the
census output that card has to draw an adjudication sample FROM. Any sample
drawn against the pre-merge instrument has to be redrawn; the two readings and
their refs are in the section above so the size of that change is known rather
than guessed.

Findings noted, ⛔ not filed here (the seat files):

- **A key mention carrying an optional marker yields no key at all.** The head of
  a span like an `allowCollapse?: boolean` annotation is `allowCollapse?`, which
  is not an identifier, so the reader returns nothing — a silent false negative
  in the same family as this card, and unchanged by it (it behaves identically
  at `57c07f002` and at `31a96ea40`). Probe: pass that span to the exported
  `keyHead` and read the null. Successor: whoever next opens this reader.
  Dedupe words: `keyHead` · optional marker · `question-mark` in a key span ·
  changeset polarity census · key extraction false negative.
- **A doc nit inside the header's POLARITY entry**, which points at the WINDOW
  PAIRING entry as "below" when it is above it. Pre-existing, untouched, nobody
  is blocked by it. Successor: none.
- **Environmental, ⛔ not a finding about this tree.** `pnpm check:node-esm-load`
  first refused with a provenance error naming another worktree of this checkout
  — turbo shares one cache across worktrees and had replayed that tree's build
  output here. After `turbo run build --force` in this worktree it exits 0.
  Successor: any agent in a sibling worktree of this container.
